messages:
mike_infra: Heads up — saw a pretty big shift to on-demand last night (about 45m). Cluster autoscaler fell back after a couple spot pools got thrashed. Anyone digging into why our fallback buffer didn't pick up earlier? :eyes:

tara_devops: Ugh. I saw the alerts. Looks like multiple spot nodegroups in us-west-2 had overlapping termination windows. ClusterAutoscaler scaled down some nodes aggressively and then flapped when spot capacity returned.

sanjay_sre: From the node / kubelet logs I pulled, termination notices hit almost simultaneously for two different instance types. We didn't stagger drain start times — everything tried to cordon+drain immediately which spiked pending pods -> CA chose on-demand.

jenna_mlinfra: That explains the throttle. We intentionally set tight drainTimeout in node lifecycle hook to be fast, but that causes many pods to be re-scheduled at once. Might want a gradual drain/backoff.

mike_infra: Agreed. Can we try a rate-limited drain orchestrator + jitter so not all tainted spot nodes start eviction at identical times? Also we should revisit the minimum on-demand spare sizing vs. expected preemption rate.

ops-bot: Incident summary: 2026-03-17 02:12 UTC - Spot churn in us-west-2 -> CA fallback to on-demand for 45m -> ~180k extra GPU-seconds billed.

tara_devops: Cost hit was notable. Also noticed some GPU workloads with tolerations for spot were landing on on-demand after CA fallback, which defeats our cost model.

sanjay_sre: Proposal: 1) Add a small rolling buffer of on-demand nodes (minAvailable for critical GPU pools) 2) Implement drain-backoff controller that enforces per-node randomized delay before eviction starts 3) Use taint-rotation: mark nodes as preemptible with a rotating priority label so CA doesn't evict entire class at once.

jenna_mlinfra: Sketch for drain-backoff controller (WIP):
```
# pseudo-config
controller:
  backoffBaseSeconds: 30
  maxJitterSeconds: 120
  ratePerRegion: 3 # nodes concurrently draining per AZ
  prioritizeBy: ["preemptiblePriority", "uptime"]
```
Controller will: cordon node, wait randomized delay, then drain pods in waves (evict small batch -> wait -> next batch) to avoid big pending spike.

mike_infra: Love it. We also need to tweak CA settings: increase expander priority for on-demand fallback and add a softMin for critical GPU nodegroups so CA prefers keeping N on-demand always.

tara_devops: Another wrinkle: our termination-notice handler currently triggers immediate pod eviction. We should change it to mark the node with taint: `node.kubernetes.io/preempting=true` and let the drain-backoff controller manage the timing. That gives us control to sequence evictions.

sanjay_sre: +1. Also add a small warm-spare spot pool with lower density (1 GPU node) per AZ that accepts longtail critical pods only — acts as a temporary buffer cheaper than on-demand but less likely to be drained en masse.

jenna_mlinfra: For cluster autoscaler we can set more conservative scale-down-utilization for spot nodegroups and a longer scale-down-delay to avoid rapid flips. Example CA flags: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-unready-time=20m --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false`.

mike_infra: We should also add a preemption budget signal into our scheduling: pods with `spotFallback: true` should have `PodDisruptionBudget` / priorityClass such that only X% of fleet is allowed to be evicted concurrently.

tara_devops: Quick config snippet for taint + toleration pattern we discussed: 
```
# node taint
kubectl taint nodes <node> spot-preemptible=true:NoExecute
# pod toleration
tolerations:
- key: "spot-preemptible"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoExecute"
```
Then drain-backoff respects that and evicts non-tolerant pods first.

sanjay_sre: Action items:
- jenna -> prototype drain-backoff controller + tests (ETA: EOD Thu)
- tara -> update termination-notice handler to taint instead of immediate eviction (ETA: tomorrow)
- mike -> add CA flag changes + minOnDemand pool proposal to infra PR (ETA: Fri)
- me -> run a chaos test in staging to validate staggered preemption handling (ETA: next week) :thumbsup:

jenna_mlinfra: I'll open a draft PR and add a simple e2e that simulates simultaneous preemption notifications and asserts throttled evictions and no spike in pending pods. Link when ready.

mike_infra: If we can get this in before next week's cost review, we might avoid another billing surprise. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: deployment mike/ca-config-changes scheduled to staging at 2026-03-18T09:00Z by mike_infra :rocket:

tara_devops: FYI adding ops runbook note for manual override: `kubectl annotate node <node> lifecycle.redwood.io/skip-drain=true` to pause controller for maintenance.

sanjay_sre: One more thought — metric to track: simultaneous-term-notice-count per AZ and percent of pods pending at peak. I'll add dashboards.

mike_infra: Great. Closing loop in #costs and will ping product with the expected savings estimate once we have numbers. :raised_hands:
